review.summary: approve_with_nits. Link checker bad 0; 83 tests pass; no [employer] or owner name left in the notes, glossary or diagrams. 1) REVIEW.md still says "He is experienced…" one line after the anonymised goal, and clashes with "they merge" elsewhere. 2) "[time zone]"/"[location]" prose survives in lesson 5.6 and in config and workflow comments although README was changed to [time zone]; STYLE.md's new rule is silent on location. 3) 17 compiled .pyc files are tracked (no .gitignore), so the PR diff carries binary churn and bytecode can carry stale text.

findings.checklist_item: Keep it anonymous: write 'the owner' or 'you' instead of a person's name
findings.title: REVIEW.md keeps a gendered pronoun right after the anonymised goal line
findings.claim: Line 43 now says 'the owner reads in order', but line 44 still says 'He is experienced with LLMs and a beginner at agents.' The same PR changed line 6 to 'request they merge' and RESPOND.md to 'they review', so the pronoun is both a leftover personal detail and inconsistent with the rest of the file.
findings.evidence: git show HEAD:REVIEW.md lines 43-44: '…that the owner reads in order, like a short book,\n  mostly on a phone in the GitHub app. He is experienced with LLMs and a beginner at agents.' Compare REVIEW.md line 6 ('request they merge') and review/RESPOND.md lines 5-6 ('they review… they merge it').
findings.proposed_change: Change 'He is experienced' to 'They are experienced' (or 'The owner is experienced'). Check with: grep -n '\bHe \|\bhe \|\bhis\b' REVIEW.md review/RESPOND.md STYLE.md README.md returns nothing.

findings.checklist_item: Keep it anonymous (new section): scope of what counts as identifying
findings.title: '[time zone]' and '[location]' prose remain after README was changed to [time zone]; STYLE rule silent on location
findings.claim: The PR treats the owner's time zone as identifying (README '[location] time' → '[time zone]') and keeps only the [time zone] machine settings. But the same wording survives as prose: lesson 5.6's exercise says '40 sites must finish by 06:00 [time zone]', and comments in review/config.yaml (lines 63, 72-73), scripts/review_harness/config.py (line 31, 'Review dates are [location] dates') and .github/workflows/review.yml (lines 33-34, '[time zone]') still name the location. The new STYLE.md section does not say whether locations and time zones count, so the weekly update has no rule to follow here.
findings.evidence: rg -n -i '[location]|\bSGT\b' weeks/ review/config.yaml scripts/review_harness/config.py .github/workflows/review.yml → week-05 line 800 '06:00 [time zone]'; config.yaml 63 '# [location] day', 72-73 '11:23 [time zone]', '13:23 [time zone]'; config.py 31; review.yml 33-34. README diff: '([location] time)' → '([time zone])'.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) apply the README standard everywhere: lesson 5.6 '06:00 local time' (the exercise does not depend on the zone), and '[time zone]' in the config.yaml, config.py and review.yml comments, keeping the TZ=[time zone] settings; or (b) decide location is not identifying and revert the README change. In both cases add one line to STYLE.md 'Keep it anonymous' saying which it is. Test: the rg command above returns only the TZ= settings and cron comments you chose to keep.

findings.title: Compiled .pyc files are tracked; the PR diff is 17 binary changes and bytecode can carry stale text
findings.claim: The repo tracks 17 __pycache__/*.pyc files and has no .gitignore. This PR therefore ships 17 binary diffs that reviewers cannot read, and the tracked bytecode duplicates source strings (the respond.py docstring is in it), so a .pyc rebuilt from an older checkout would re-commit the removed wording. The ones in HEAD are current (0 hits for the old name, 1 for 'the owner merges'), but only because the author happened to re-run the tests before committing. The 312 bytecode now present as untracked files shows the churn will continue.
findings.evidence: git ls-files | grep -c pycache → 17; cat .gitignore → no such file; git show HEAD:scripts/review_harness/__pycache__/respond.cpython-313.pyc | strings | grep -c '[owner]' → 0; grep -c 'the owner merges' → 1; git status shows 11 untracked *.cpython-312.pyc files.
findings.proposed_change: In this PR or a follow-up: git rm -r --cached scripts/review_harness/__pycache__ scripts/review_harness/providers/__pycache__ tests/__pycache__; add a .gitignore with '__pycache__/' and '*.pyc'. Test: python -m pytest -q tests still passes and git status shows no .pyc after a run.

findings.checklist_item: Keep it anonymous: no real person named
findings.title: Test fixture still names the owner; anonymising it does not affect the tests
findings.claim: The PR leaves the owner's name in the fixture header ('Decided by: [owner]…', '(author; for [owner] to confirm)') because it is a copied sample. The tests only read the table rows and the '| ID |' header line, so the prose can be anonymised exactly as reviews/decisions.md was without changing any test behaviour. Leaving it means the name is still greppable in the repo one commit after a PR whose purpose was to remove it.
findings.evidence: tests/test_review_harness.py: test_live_log_has_the_same_format compares only the line starting with '| ID |'; table_rows(), decided() and row_prefix() in respond.py parse rows starting with '|' and skip the header/separator. rg -n '[owner]' tests/fixtures/decisions_sample.md → lines 10, 11, 18, 19.
findings.proposed_change: Apply the same three edits as in reviews/decisions.md lines 10-19 to the fixture ('the owner'). Test: python -m pytest -q tests → 83 passed.

findings.checklist_item: Plain language: a list of parallel items becomes one bulleted list
findings.title: New anonymity bullet in REVIEW.md is split off from the 'Pay most attention to' list by a blank line
findings.claim: The new bullet is separated from the preceding list by an empty line, so Markdown renders it as a second, one-item list and it reads as an orphan rather than as the last item of 'Pay most attention to:'.
findings.evidence:
Diff hunk @@ -81,6 +81,9 @@: '  week, "*Answer coming…"…

+- anything that identifies the owner, an employer…
+  at least `major`.
+
 Stay out of taste'.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the blank line 83 so the bullet joins the list.

findings.title: respond.yml comment capitalises 'The owner' mid-sentence
findings.claim: The replacement kept the original capital letter from the name, so the comment reads '…nothing counts until\n# The owner merges it.'
findings.evidence: Diff: '-# [owner] merges it.' → '+# The owner merges it.' following 'nothing counts until' on the previous line.
findings.proposed_change: Lower-case to '# the owner merges it.'
